name: TX-26
label: Safe R

key_factors: Gill has raised $4.2 million with $1.4 million on hand; Democrat Steven Shook has raised about $17,000
District leans Republican by roughly 11 points and Gill is the incumbent
Prediction markets price Gill's reelection near 98 percent
No public polls or expert ratings exist for this race
model.rationale: Gill holds an R+11 district and has built a massive financial advantage over an opponent who has raised almost nothing, while markets price his reelection at about 98 percent. With no competitive polling, the structural evidence points to a comfortable Republican hold.
model.watch: A late influx of Democratic or outside spending, or a sharply favorable national environment for the out-party, could narrow the margin.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Brandon Gill, a first-term Republican, seeks reelection in a North Texas district that leans Republican by about eleven points. He enters the general election with an overwhelming financial edge, having raised more than $4 million and holding $1.4 million on hand. His Democratic opponent, Steven Shook, has raised roughly $17,000, and a Libertarian candidate is also on the ballot. No public polls or expert ratings are available for this race.

Prediction markets give Gill about a 98 percent chance of winning, and the district's partisan lean combined with his incumbency and fundraising advantage points to a wide margin. The main uncertainty is the absence of polling, which leaves the exact size of the victory open, but the available evidence points to a safe Republican hold.
